From straight above (integrated-sea-from-above) the water is neutral warm grey, (37,36,35) at the nadir and (79,76,71) obliquely, with no blue or green of a water body at all and a uniform sandpaper grain: wet asphalt. With the capsule hanging over it the scene reads as a salt flat or a desert at dusk. findings.realReference: sea-surface-close/rough-sea-nato.jpg: under overcast the sea is dark blue-grey (85,95,104), 0.2x the sky (207,211,215). A water surface under a diffuse sky can never be brighter than the sky it mirrors (Fresnel reflectance is at most 1 and about 0.02-0.1 at the angles of the middle distance). dragon-crs1-splashdown.jpg and apollo17-splashdown.jpg: seen from above the sea keeps a blue to slate-blue body colour.
findings.likelyCause: The mirror term ignores the cloud deck. src/render/ocean/shaders/waterBrdf.ts brdfWaterAmbient (lines 817-826) takes spec from waterSkyRadiance (696 ff.), which returns the env probe or the clear-sky view table within 50 km and the clear-sky irradiance / pi beyond; the cloud light of surfaceWgsl.ts 886-930 (cl.x, cl.y, cloudBase) only scales the diffuse ambient (amb.skyIrradiance) and the direct sun. So under a deck the sea mirrors the bright, warm, unobscured sky near a low sun that the viewer cannot see, and the white cloud-base term lifts the body on top. Second candidate to rule out in the same run: cl.x not reaching zero under this deck, so that the glitter's sheen share spreads the sun over the whole sea. The integration lab's older picture (out/screens/integration/budget-splashdown.png, 11-11) had a navy sea under the same kind of deck, so this came in with the cloud-light work of rounds 1-2.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean, with atmosphere-clouds and sky-lighting for the input. The sea must mirror what is drawn above it: either sample an environment probe that contains the cloud deck (request to sky-lighting if the probe is cloudless), or attenuate waterSkyRadiance by the deck's sky visibility in the mirrored direction and add the cloud base's radiance there (the same cl the ambient uses), near and far alike. Verify cl.x is 0 under a closed deck. Add a check to integrated.spec: under overcast, mean sea luminance in the band under the horizon is at most 0.7x the sky band above it and the near water at most 0.25x; the nadir colour has B > R. Re-shoot integrated-* and judge against rough-sea-nato.

findings.defect: The round-1 blocker in its new form. From 3 km to 100 km the slicks are drawn as line art: bundles of 3 to 8 hairlines of constant one-pixel width, evenly spaced and exactly parallel, curving together like the contours of a topographic map, wood grain or a fingerprint; dark outside the glint's core and white inside it. Where the flow has an eddy they close into concentric rings (read as ripples from a thrown stone at 3-5 km) or into a pen-drawn loop (16 km, 30 km), and at a saddle they make a hairpin. Between the bundles the glint is a smooth airbrushed gradient with soft cloud-like mottling, so the lines sit on it like ink on paper. At the lab's 7 m/s wind there would be next to no slicks at all.
findings.realReference: earth-orbit-ocean/ship-wake-glint.jpg and gulf-oil-slick-glint.jpg: slicks are marbled swirls and feathered streamers of every width from hairlines to broad patches, braiding, merging and fraying, dense in some regions and absent in others, with structure at all scales; never sets of equidistant lines. Surface films are broken up above about 5-6 m/s; what a 7 m/s sea shows from the air is fine wind streaks along the wind, whitecap specks and cloud shadows (glint-from-aircraft-hawaii.jpg: a grainy path with ragged edges).
findings.likelyCause: src/render/ocean/fieldModel.ts and its WGSL twin in waterBrdf.ts (lines ~244-252, lineBundle / lineDense): the filaments are the level lines of the stream function psi at integer steps, switched on in bundles of consecutive levels. Level lines of a smooth scalar field at equal steps are by construction parallel, equidistant, closed around extrema and hairpinned at saddles: a contour plot. Width is the width in psi over the current speed, which keeps each line at about a pixel. No dependence on wind speed.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean. Stop drawing iso-levels. Either advect a multi-octave tracer along the flow (a few steps of line-integral convolution of noise along the streamlines gives filaments that braid, fray and vary in width), or keep psi but draw slick AREA: threshold a noise that is stretched along the flow, with widths over two decades, feathered edges, strength varying along the line with drop-outs, no closed curves near extrema of psi. Scale the whole slick contrast with wind: full below 3 m/s, gone by 6-7 m/s; at 7 m/s replace it with weak wind streaks along the wind and the mesoscale gust mottling. Judge alt10k and alt30k next to ship-wake-glint and glint-from-aircraft-hawaii at the same size.

findings.defect: From 3 km to orbit the glint is matte paint, never light. No pixel clips anywhere: the core is cream (192,183,162) with a maximum of 195/255 at 3 km, 200 at 10 km, 210 at 30 km, 195 at 100 km, and neutral grey (150,145,142), Y 0.28, maximum 165 from LEO. From LEO the glint is a dim grey mottled column that reads as a fog bank or frosted glass rather than sunlight on water, and glint-leo.png is unchanged from round 1 at 4.3:1 (core Y 0.255, sea (44,68,112) Y 0.059). findings.realReference: earth-orbit-ocean/glint-from-aircraft-hawaii.jpg: the path is clipped white (Y 1.0), made of grain, with ragged edges that break into sparkle, over a sea at Y 0.016. florida-bahamas-glint.jpg and glint-pacific-cb-shadows.jpg: from orbit the core is white to warm white, Y 0.32-0.61 with p95 0.73 and clipped centres, (209,184,145) to (232,220,203), a broad ellipse; never mid-grey.
findings.likelyCause: Two things. (a) Ocean: above about 1 km the whole Cox-Munk variance is in the lobe's roughness (the Poisson count has become its mean, the 'sheen share'), so the image is the smooth mean radiance; the tilting of the lobe by the waves a pixel nearly resolves (1-10 m, the far-wave bank) is too weak to break the path into grain or to fray its edge. (b) Exposure and tone curve (sky-lighting / core): the meter exposes for the glint itself and the shoulder holds it at 0.45-0.5 display, so the brightest thing in the frame can never reach white. From LEO the core is additionally desaturated to neutral by the air's path radiance.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean for (a), sky-lighting / core for (b). (a) Keep variance in the picture: evaluate the lobe per pixel on the far-wave bank's slopes with only the sub-footprint variance left in the roughness, and keep a residual sparkle (count variance of the 1-10 m facets) until the footprint exceeds about 50 m, so the path is grain at 3 km and frays at its edge at 10 km. (b) Let the meter ignore the top few percent of the frame (or cap the weight of specular pixels) so the core clips as in every photograph; check that the tone curve's white point is reachable by a 20-40x highlight. Then re-aim glint-leo to the oblique geometry of leo.png or drop it from the picture set. Target: at least 0.5 % of the core clipped at 3-10 km; LEO core Y above 0.5 and warm (R > B by 20 or more).

findings.defect: Whitecaps are stamped decals. From 120-500 m each one is a compact teardrop or blob 2-5 m across (aspect about 2:1) with a blunt head and a short taper, all of one size class, all pointing the same way, filled with one flat off-white (199,196,191) behind a crisp edge, with a few pure-dark single pixels inside. None is a crescent across the wind, none trails a streak, there is no old foam fading between them and no population of small ones. They read as ice chunks or dabs of paint. From 2-3 m the one in frame is a flat white lozenge with a hard outline lying on the water like a sticker (no thickness, no lit front, no lace behind). The count is now right for the wind from above, which is a real gain; the shape and age are not.
findings.realReference: sea-surface-close/rough-sea-nato.jpg: whitecaps are elongated streaks (4-8:1 at a grazing view) with hard bright cores and translucent greenish tails; beaufort-6.jpg and orion-eft1-floating.jpg: many small short crests of mixed size with a sharp leading edge; heavy-seas-essex-1960 (INDEX): fresh foam bright and sharp, old foam decaying into a lace of thin filaments.
findings.likelyCause: Foam is injected where the cascades' breaking criterion (Jacobian over a sigma threshold, now 2.53) is exceeded, which marks compact spots where crests of several cascades cross; the hold that makes a breaker travel with its crest is off (foamHoldDropSigma 0, hand-off 15.1), so nothing moves with a crest or leaves a trail; decay is isotropic and quick; the fill is the one-albedo foam layer with an alpha-tested edge. The dark pixels are holes of the lace at single-pixel size.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean. Make a breaker a short segment ALONG a crest of the dominant wind-sea cascade (direction from that cascade's gradient), 3-8:1, travelling at phase speed for 0.5-1 period, and let the foam map keep what it leaves: thick foam e-folding in 3-5 s, thin lace in 10-20 s, stretched down the wind. Keep small ones (a power-law of lengths from 0.5 to 15 m) so the hold does not concentrate the coverage in two big patches, which is what stopped the last attempt; calibrate count and coverage together in foam.spec (it now measures against a local background). Shade the front brighter than the trail and filter the lace so no single-pixel holes are left.

findings.defect: From 1-3 m the sea has no wave faces. It is a field of low rounded hummocks with a fine ripple texture on them; nothing rises to hide the trough behind it, the foot of the capsule or the floats, and the horizon is a ruled line in every near-surface frame. For a 7 m/s wind this is a Beaufort 2 sea with whitecaps pasted on. In stability-animated the foreground detail is also stretched into pale streaks that fan out from the bottom centre of the frame.
findings.realReference: sea-surface-close/orion-eft1-floating.jpg and beaufort-6.jpg: short-crested steep wavelets with distinct lit and dark faces at the 1-3 m scale riding on the swell, crests that overlap one another toward the horizon and break its line; rough-sea-nato.jpg: a jagged horizon of wave backs.
findings.likelyCause: Data, by the lead's decision: the rendered heights are the physics swell (eight components), and the wind sea of the FFT cascades is kept small against it; steepness (ka) of the 1-5 m waves is too low to make faces. The fan of streaks is the short cascades' normal detail seen at a few centimetres per pixel right under the camera, stretched by the horizontal displacement.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: simulation data (wave heights for the wind) and the lead; ocean for the visual part. Give the wind sea its own amplitude for the wind speed (Hs about 1 m of short-period sea at 7 m/s on top of the swell) either in the physics' wave query or as a visual-only band above the wavelength the buoyancy samples (shorter than about 3 m, where it cannot move the capsule's waterline beyond the 5 cm tolerance), with choppiness high enough for ka 0.2-0.3. Judge midday against orion-eft1-floating: at least a few crests must cut the horizon and hide a float.

findings.defect: The water now answers a splash, but the answer reads as an ice floe. At +0.2 s two flat white triangular flaps stand beside the hull like paper fins and no cavity is legible. From +1 s a flat, opaque, matte off-white pancake (178,174,166), Y 0.42, max 190/255, with a torn hard rim surrounds the hull; it keeps GROWING to about 600 px at +10 s and is as opaque and white then as at +1 s. It has no bright boiling centre, no radial streaks, no thinning to lace, and the water inside and around it is the same navy: no milky turquoise of aerated water. The orange floats disappear into it. The ring waves measured in the spec (0.1-0.2 m) cannot be seen in any of the four stills. And the sequence has only been drawn in the ocean lab on a grey cone: no picture anywhere shows it with the real capsule and the vfx crown and spray (the vfx lab's own pictures, out/screens/vfx/splash, are on a flat blue stand-in plane and predate the response).
findings.realReference: Splashdown footage and sea-surface-close/dragon-crs1-splashdown.jpg, orion-eft1-floating.jpg: after the crown falls back the capsule sits in a ring of white foam over pale green-turquoise aerated water; within about 10-20 s the white breaks into lace and streaks and the turquoise fades, leaving a thin foam line at the hull.
findings.likelyCause: The foam patch is written into the foam map at full coverage with a radius that spreads and a long life, and is shaded by the same one-albedo foam layer as the surf; no term for bubbles under the surface (the body's scattering is unchanged inside the patch); the cavity and rings are small against the swell and get no shading emphasis; the FakeSim of the integration lab emits no 'splash', so the combined picture could not be made.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean, with vfx for the crown and core-support for the lab event. Give the patch a life: coverage peaks at 0.5-1.5 s, then the solid core shrinks while a lace ring expands and thins (e-fold 4-6 s; gone as a solid by 10 s); add a bubble plume term that raises the water body's scattering to a milky pale turquoise under and just outside the foam, fading over 10-20 s; break the rim radially. Let the integration lab fire a 'splash' at the real capsule and shoot 0.2, 1, 3 and 10 s with vfx on; judge those four against the splashdown references.

findings.defect: There is still no surf zone. On the lab beach the run-up is a flat white sheet with a hard edge lying on the sand, next to a dull grey band and isolated grey patches on dry sand that are not connected to the sea (the thin run-up film fighting the beach surface); offshore of it there are one or two torn white patches and then open water: no rows of breakers, no lacy foam between them, no backwash lines, and no wet sand. From the sea (shore, shore-1440p) the beach is met by a faint white thread. At the real coast (integration lab, lava shore) the surf is a thin white chalk outline that hugs the rock, with a few slightly wider dabs.
findings.realReference: earth-terrain-aerial/helicopter-ocean-oahu.jpg: several parallel breaker lines, each a broad white band with a sharp leading edge and a lacy, streaked trailing side, green-turquoise water between them. kalapana-coast.jpg: at a lava cliff a turbulent white apron tens of metres wide over pale aerated water, with foam streaks trailing off. punaluu-black-sand.jpg: a lacy swash edge and a dark, glossy band of wet sand behind it.
findings.likelyCause: Bores are drawn in stretches where a swell crest exceeds what the depth can carry, and their foam decays before the next one; with the lab's steep bed the zone where that holds is a few metres wide, and at a rocky shore the depth band is narrower still. The swash is a water film with a white edge drawn where the film is millimetres thick, so it z-fights the sand in patches. Wet sand is terrain shading (request ocean-7, open).
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean for the surf, terrain for the wet band (ocean-7). Define the surf zone by depth below about 1.3 times the local breaker height and keep broken-wave foam alive across the whole of it: a bright front per crest, lace that persists until the next row. At steep or rocky shores (bed slope above about 0.1) add an impact apron whose width scales with the swell height, with the aerated-water tint of the splash finding. Bias the run-up film against the bed and fade it by thickness so it cannot leave patches; hand terrain the run-up's maximum line for the wet band.

findings.view: out/screens/ocean/shoreAlong.png (0-420 x 400-700; comb of teeth 40-83 x 472-483), out/screens/ocean/splash-impact-3s.png, out/screens/ocean/splash-impact-10s.png, out/screens/ocean/stability-animated.png (600-655 x 360-378), out/screens/ocean/coast60.png, out/screens/ocean/perf-coast-1440p.png
findings.defect: Foam as a material is still paper. Within 5-30 m of the camera every foam patch is one flat matte off-white, (182,178,170) in shoreAlong, never above 190/255 in full sun, with a crisp outline and holes punched through to the water. There are no bubbles or cells at any scale, no bright thick core grading to a thin translucent rim, no relief or self-shadow that can be seen, no wet sheen. One edge in shoreAlong carries a regular comb of teeth. It is brighter than the sand now (Y 0.45 against 0.34), which fixes the worst of round 1, but next to a photograph it is white paint or papier-mache.
findings.realReference: sea-surface-close/rough-sea-nato.jpg and INDEX (heavy-seas-essex-1960): fresh foam is brilliant white (it clips) with a sharp edge, thins through a reticulated lace of filaments and bubble rafts to green-white translucent water; punaluu-black-sand.jpg: the swash edge is a lace a few centimetres thick with visible cells.
findings.likelyCause: waterFoamAlbedo and the foam layer in src/render/ocean/shaders/waterBrdf.ts and surfaceWgsl.ts: one albedo (0.8 thin) times sky and sun irradiance, coverage from a thresholded lace at one scale, opacity cut hard at the threshold; the lace's relief normal is too weak to shade. The exposure holds diffuse white at about 0.45. The comb is the foam map's texel edge sampled without filtering along a steep gradient.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean. Drive albedo and opacity by thickness (thick 0.9 and opaque; lace 0.5 and half transparent; the last rim only a tint), add two finer lace octaves down to bubble rafts of 2-10 cm within 10 m of the eye, erode the edge with that noise instead of a hard threshold, light it with its own relief and a broad wet highlight, and let thick sunlit foam reach display white. Sample the foam map bilinearly (or bicubically) where it is magnified.

findings.view: out/screens/ocean/splash-1440p.png (native 780-1000 x 690-960), out/screens/ocean/perf-splash-1440p.png (native 787-966 x 698-775), out/screens/ocean/splash.png (390-500 x 360-510), out/screens/ocean/splash-impact-0.2s.png (392-485 x 357-400)
findings.defect: The capsule's mirror image is a box. Under the hull lies a pale grey column of constant width with straight vertical sides, about one and a half hull heights long, evenly lighter than the sea (Y 0.083 against 0.038 beside it) and bounded by a rim of regular halftone dots; inside it the dither pattern is visible at 2x. The hull is a cone, so its image should be widest at the waterline and narrow downward, and it should be torn into horizontal dashes by the waves; instead a translucent rectangle hangs under the capsule. No aqua glow of the submerged part, no darkening of the water at the hull's foot. Floats and markers still have no image at all.
findings.realReference: sea-surface-close/artemis2-floating.jpg and orion-eft1-floating.jpg: the reflection is short, broken into wavering horizontal fragments, follows the hull's shape and colour (the red of the bags is recognisable), and fades within about one hull height; the water at the hull's foot is a shade lighter and greener.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/ocean/shaders/surfaceWgsl.ts lines 1032-1078: the hull is met as an upright cylinder about the vessel's axis, with seven slopes that turn the ray only up and down and are shifted per pixel by up to half their spacing. A cylinder gives a constant-width column; the per-pixel shift gives the dithered rim; one flat hull radiance gives the even fill.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean (vehicle supplies the profile). Meet the ray with the vessel's real outline, at least radius as a function of height (a cone frustum for the capsule), and take the radiance from the hull point hit (the lit scene colour where it is in the frame, else the vessel's albedo times its lighting). Spread the seven slopes sideways as well, drop the per-pixel shift in favour of the resolved wave normal so the image breaks into dashes, and fade it with distance from the waterline. Add the tint of the submerged hull seen through the water.

findings.view: out/screens/ocean/handover-refraction.png (speckle band 100-1180 x 360-600; blotches 0-1280 x 600-720), out/screens/ocean/refraction.png (speckle 100-1180 x 360-600; blotches 0-1280 x 600-720), out/screens/ocean/shoreAlong.png (700-1280 x 480-720)
findings.defect: Shallow water is a saturated pool-turquoise paint with noise in it. The colour is one teal, (14,108,100) to (39,102,93), from the swash edge to the shelf's lip; it does not thin to clear water over pale sand in the last metres. The bed has no detail (no ripples, no grain). The caustics are soft pale blotches like camouflage near the camera rather than a net of thin bright lines, and beyond the first few metres the whole surface is covered in fine cyan single-pixel speckle, which will crawl in motion: mean horizontal pixel-to-pixel luma change 9.4-15.4 in handover-refraction rows 360-600 (round 1 measured 11.2 there: unchanged), 4.4-8.3 in refraction, 3.6-5.4 in shoreAlong's shallows, against 2.9-3.5 in deep water at the same range (midday, splash) and 2.5 in the rows just below, so the grain also starts at a visible line near row 600. The submerged ball still sits on a small dark saucer.
findings.realReference: earth-orbit-ocean/bahamas-shallows.jpg and mataiva-atoll.jpg (INDEX): shallow water colour is the bottom seen through water, pale turquoise to green-white (113,168,168), (126,158,146), changing 1.5-2x over sharp sinuous edges of the bed; punaluu-black-sand.jpg: at the edge the water is clear and the bed shows. A caustic net is thin, sharp, bright lines that swim.
findings.likelyCause: Body colour from a depth-only absorption with a uniform bed albedo (the lab's sand has no texture and the ocean adds none); the caustic term is the foam lace reused as a net times the cascades' focusing, low in contrast and not band-limited to the pixel's footprint, so beyond a few metres it aliases into speckle together with the per-pixel refraction offset on unresolved ripples.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean; terrain for bed detail on real coasts. Band-limit the net and the refraction offset by the pixel footprint (pre-filtered levels; fade to the mean where a cell is under two pixels). Sharpen the net near the eye (a ridge function of the lace, not its value). Let the bed's own albedo and a sand-ripple normal show through in the first metre of depth and desaturate the water toward the bed colour there. Check the speckle with the mean horizontal pixel difference in the mid-field (it should be within 1.5x of deep water at the same range).

findings.view: out/screens/ocean/shore.png (straight band edges across the full width near y 575-600 and y 630-655), out/screens/ocean/shore-1440p.png (native y ~1160 and ~1260), out/screens/ocean/coast60.png (about eight diagonal stripes over 130-730 x 480-720, parallel to the shelf), out/screens/ocean/perf-coast-1440p.png (native 450-1150 x 1020-1400)
findings.defect: New in this round's pictures: the water colour over the shelf changes in steps. Straight-edged bands of constant colour run along lines of equal depth: three wide horizontal terraces across the foreground of the shore views (the red channel of the row mean drops from 12 to 5 within a few rows at y ~592-604) and a fan of alternating lighter and darker stripes over the teal-to-navy transition from 60 m. Visible at normal size in shore-1440p as ruled lines across the water; unmistakable with the contrast raised.
findings.realReference: Water over a sloping bed grades continuously from turquoise to navy (earth-orbit-ocean/quirimbas-islands.jpg, bahamas-shallows.jpg); steps follow real bed features, never straight contour lines.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/ocean/shaders/surfaceWgsl.ts lines 876-878: 's.param = mix(round(enc * 255.0) / 255.0, enc, detail)' - the body depth is rounded to the 8 bits the far sheet's G-buffer carries wherever the wave detail has faded, and the body colour is a steep function of that depth between about 3 and 30 m, so each code is a visible terrace.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean (and core if the G-buffer channel is the limit). In the forward pass use the exact depth for the colour everywhere it is known and keep the rounding only for the hand-over band's equality test; for the far sheet either dither the encoding by half a code with the frame's blue noise before rounding, re-space encodeWaterDepth so that codes are densest between 0 and 40 m, or carry the depth in 16 bits. Add a check: no step larger than 1/255 between adjacent rows of the row-mean over the shelf in shore.png.

findings.view: out/screens/ocean/markers-with-chop.png (700-1200 x 560-720), out/screens/ocean/markers-swell-only.png (300-1200 x 400-720), out/screens/ocean/midday.png (380-760 x 610-720)
findings.defect: Within a few metres of a low camera the lit glitter cells are visible as squares. In markers-with-chop (eye 1.1 m) the highlights are white quadrilateral tiles 8-20 px across with straight edges, like mosaic or shards of glass, some still with a dim outline around a dark interior; on the mirror-flat sea of markers-swell-only the whole glitter is a perspective grid of white rectangles, where a flat sea would show one image of the sun. At 2.2 m (midday) they are small round beads, which pass. This is the view from the capsule's window after splashdown.
findings.realReference: sea-surface-close/orion-eft1-floating.jpg, apollo9-floats.jpg: near glints are thin curved streaks and crescents that follow the ripple crests, with bloom; nothing has straight edges.
findings.likelyCause: The count of lit facets is drawn per world-space cell with one random number per cell (waterBrdf.ts, cells around lines 149-173 and 528-546); the smallest cell is larger than a pixel close to the eye, so a lit cell is a lit square. The weight that should switch the draw off where the shading normal carries the slopes does not reach zero at 1 m, and on a sea without chop the capillary remainder still draws.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean. Choose the cell level from the pixel footprint so a cell is never wider than about a pixel, or fade the count draw out completely where it would be, leaving the highlight to the resolved normal with the capillary remainder as roughness. Shape what remains by the facet's lobe, not the cell's footprint. With no wind sea at all, mirror the sun's disc.

findings.view: out/screens/ocean/handover-near-on.png against out/screens/ocean/handover-near-off.png (420-780 x 520-720; measured over 300-1000 x 450-720), out/screens/ocean/alt3k.png (300-800 x 420-720), out/screens/ocean/alt10k-1440p.png and perf-10km-1440p.png (lower half of the glint), out/screens/ocean/climb-4796m.png
findings.defect: At 6 km the two passes still draw different water at the same pixels: with the near field on, the glint is crisp fine ribs of wave trains; with it off, the far sheet shows soft out-of-focus lumps and a few blurred bright dashes. Mean absolute difference 7.9/255 over the glint (7.8 in round 1), p99 39, max 113; the frame above row 437 is identical and the slick arcs agree. As the near field fades out between 6 and 9 km the sea therefore goes out of focus over a few seconds of ascent and snaps back into focus on the way down. On its own, the far sheet's texture from 3 to 10 km is an embossed, evenly sized bump relief (hammered metal, orange peel) lit from one side.
findings.realReference: From an airliner the sea is fine sharp grain at every altitude, crossed by long straight swell lines; it never looks defocused (earth-orbit-ocean/glint-from-aircraft-hawaii.jpg; sea-surface-close/dragon-crs1-splashdown.jpg for the wave trains from a few hundred metres).
findings.likelyCause: The near field is the FFT cascades with their full spectrum up to 0.98 fadeStart; the far sheet is a bank of 14 components limited by the footprint, which keeps only the long ones, so its slope spectrum at the pixel scale is far below the near field's at the same place. The single-pixel hand-over fixed in 15.4 was the glitter; the wave detail itself was only looked at.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean. Match the slope variance per octave on both sides of the fade: give the far sheet two or three footprint-filtered detail normal layers taken from the cascades' own normal maps (rotated and warped against tiling) between 3 and 12 km, weighted so that at fadeStart the luminance power spectrum of near-off is within 20 % of near-on per octave down to two pixels. Add that spectrum comparison to the hand-over spec next to the pixel difference.

findings.view: out/screens/terrain/integrated-200m.png (860-1920 x 250-335)
findings.defect: In the integration lab's coast view four or five dead-straight pale lines run across the whole far sea parallel to the horizon, each ending exactly at the shore, with the water a shade lighter on one side of each. At first sight they read as scan lines or a level-of-detail boundary; they are probably the roughness field's fronts seen at a grazing angle.
findings.realReference: Convergence lines and swell crests seen low over the sea are long but wavering, broken and of uneven strength (earth-terrain-aerial/helicopter-ocean-oahu.jpg: swell lines bend and fade).
findings.likelyCause: The 'fronts' of the roughness field (single long lines with a feathered side, fieldModel.ts) have no curvature at the kilometre scale, no breaks and full contrast outside the glint.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean. Give fronts finite length, meander and drop-outs, and scale their contrast with the specular weight so they fade outside the glint and at grazing angles. Confirm in the lab with the field's debug view that these lines are fronts and not a pass boundary.

findings.view: out/screens/ocean/markers-swell-only.png (spheres 160-1120 x 315-370), out/screens/ocean/markers-with-chop.png (160-1120 x 315-370), out/screens/ocean/splash-impact-10s.png
findings.defect: Carried from round 1: floating things that are not registered vessels (the marker floats; by extension chutes on the water, buoys, a pier, the pad seen across the water) have no mirror image even on a mirror-flat sea, no broken streak with chop and no lap ring at their waterline.
findings.realReference: sea-surface-close/dragon-crs1-splashdown.jpg, apollo9-floats.jpg: the floating canopies have dark smeared reflections and a disturbed rim of water.
findings.likelyCause: Only vessel slots are met by the reflection rays; there is no screen-space or probe fallback for other geometry.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean. A cheap screen-space march along the mirrored ray for whatever is in the opaque colour buffer above the waterline (two or three taps on the resolved normal), fading at the frame's edge; the vessel path stays for the hull.

findings.view: out/screens/ocean/down150.png (100-500 x 100-400), out/screens/ocean/foam-coverage-150m.png, out/screens/terrain/integrated-200m.png (1100-1900 x 600-1000)
findings.defect: Looked down on from 150-200 m the open sea is a very fine uniform grain with no readable wave trains or groups, and its colour is an ultramarine, (20,45,91), with green at 0.49 of blue.
findings.realReference: sea-surface-close/apollo17-splashdown.jpg and dragon-crs1-splashdown.jpg: from a few hundred metres the wave trains and their crossing pattern are plainly visible; INDEX: calm open ocean from above is navy (27-40, 62-77, 95-116), green at about 0.65 of blue.
findings.likelyCause: Low amplitude of the 5-30 m waves (see the wave-shape finding) and a body scattering colour with too little green.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean (colour), simulation data (heights). Raise the green of the deep-water body colour toward the measured navy; the pattern follows from the wind-sea amplitude.

findings.view: out/screens/ocean/alt3k.png, alt10k.png, alt30k.png, perf-10km-1440p.png (sea beside the glint; salmon bar at the horizon end of the column, native 1130-1430 x 165-205)
findings.defect: Outside the glint the sea from 3 to 30 km is a perfectly smooth navy gradient: no whitecap specks, no wind streaks, no mottling; and the far end of the glint column is capped by a flat-topped salmon bar with hard left and right ends at the horizon.
findings.realReference: earth-orbit-ocean/glint-from-aircraft-hawaii.jpg: the dark sea beside the path still carries grain, streaks and cloud shadows; the path dissolves into the horizon haze without an edge.
findings.likelyCause: The roughness field only shows where the specular term is strong; whitecaps are not carried into the far sheet's albedo above a few kilometres; the lobe is cut where the mirror direction leaves the sun's elevation range at the horizon.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean; atmosphere for cloud shadows. Feed the statistical whitecap coverage and the gust mottling into the far sheet's diffuse term (a 1-3 % brightness texture), and feather the lobe's end into the horizon.

findings.view: out/screens/ocean/alt500.png (core 520-760 x 430-640)
findings.defect: At 500 m the path sparkles convincingly at normal size, but only 0.004 % of the core's pixels clip and its median is a mid-grey (90,87,86): a dense grey grain with rare whites rather than white points on dark water.
findings.realReference: earth-orbit-ocean/glint-from-aircraft-hawaii.jpg: the core of the path is clipped white; the grain shows at its edges.
findings.likelyCause: The sheen share of the many faint facets carries most of the energy at this footprint, and the exposure sits on the path.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: ocean, sky-lighting for the meter. Shift energy from the sheen share to the counted facets up to about 1 km, and see the exposure point of the glint finding.
